method: All 70 exact live article webpages individually opened. Selected Presentation or named Commentaires passages read, not all hosted author panels or original print editions. Historical claims are observations requiring independent confirmation.

sourceQualityIssues.issue: H2 says Navigation despite article content about St Clet and St Marcellinus; indexed title preserved with correction field.
Fourth Advent week pages repeat a template text mentioning third Advent week and St Thomas December 21; editorial anomaly, no canonical rubrical correction.
Shared introductory Marian Saturday history; do not count five independent attestations or merge five seasonal formularies.
Old/new Common articles repeat Parsch commentary; no evidence of independent corroboration or interchangeable Mass formularies.

records.observedSourceTopic: Local September 17 Saint Epvre account records bishop of Toul, the Saint-Maurice church later associated with his abbey, and a 978 elevation of his relics.
Presentation distinguishes John Leonardi's October 9 Roman observance and the stronger local observance of St Denis in France; it also hosts Benedict XVI's 2009 catechesis.
The May 31 Queenship of Mary page dates the feast's institution to Pius XII in 1954 and features a Dom Gaspard Lefebvre meditation on Marian intercession.

records.sourceTitle: Mardi de la 2ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.observedSourceTopic: Guéranger's Second Advent Tuesday text contrasts Lucifer's pride with the Incarnation's divine humility; it is devotional interpretation rather than a Mass Proper.

records.sourceTitle: Vendredi de la 2ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.observedSourceTopic: Guéranger's Second Advent Friday commentary depicts paganism and the Gentile response to Christ, with markedly period-specific generalisations.

records.sourceTitle: Samedi de la 2ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.observedSourceTopic: The Second Advent Saturday commentary uses Mary as the humble valley where Christ is received, associating Advent prophecy with Marian devotion.
The local Translation of St Mansuy reuses his ordinary feast readings but claims three proper orations and a distinct shorter Gospel of the Sadducees; abbey foundation history is included.
The host explicitly reports suppression of the Sacred Heart octave in 1955 and replaces unavailable Guéranger original octave commentary with other authors and older Mass meditations.
The Nicolas of Tolentino page includes a Francis de Sales habit-and-profession sermon dated September 10, 1620, not just biographical notes about the Augustinian saint.

records.displayedTitleCorrection: Article about Sts Clet and Marcellinus; site heading is Navigation
records.observedSourceTopic: Live article heading incorrectly reads Navigation, but its presentation and Mass texts concern Saints Clet and Marcellinus on April 26, noting the Clet/Anaclet calendar distinction.
The Eleutherius page says the Liber Pontificalis supplies a burial day without initially identifying him as martyr; the martyr title appears in later Lateran/Vatican calendars.
The newer page for Margaret of Scotland records her death and later feast development; Guéranger connects her Christian queenship to that of Clotilde.
The diocesan biography of Augustin Schœffler covers German-speaking upbringing, Lorraine seminary training and departure for the Tonkin mission.
The Wenceslas page combines an early Czech-prince history with a 2009 homily of Benedict XVI on the martyr's example to rulers.

records.sourceTitle: St Placide et ses Compagnons, martyrs
records.observedSourceTopic: The presentation explicitly distinguishes Sicilian martyrs from a much later Benedictine narrative identifying their Placid with St Benedict's disciple.

records.sourceTitle: Sts Denis, évêque, Rustique et Eleuthère, martyrs
records.observedSourceTopic: The French St Denis article says his local feast outranks John Leonardi in some dioceses and identifies the Denis-of-Paris/Areopagite/mystical-writer equation as a ninth-century legend.

records.sourceTitle: Sᵗᵉ Marguerite d’Ecosse, reine et veuve
records.observedSourceTopic: An older article carries substantially the same Margaret of Scotland 10 June presentation and Guéranger reflection as the newer Margaret page.
The Joseph the Worker page recounts the 1955 institution replacing the Patronage feast but inserts a strongly negative editorial judgment on pastoral motivation.

records.sourceTitle: St Léonard de Port-Maurice, conf. (messe en certains lieux, suppl. du Missel)
records.observedSourceTopic: Leonard of Port Maurice's November 26 Mass is expressly marked as available in the pro aliquibus locis supplement; the lengthy biographical narrative is not a universal proper.

records.sourceTitle: 6ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Toussaint
records.observedSourceTopic: The sixth day of the former All Saints octave includes Guéranger on Alleluia in Greek and Mozarabic funeral traditions, plus reports of earlier patristic testimony.
A Verdun-only account identifies Saint Airy as Agericus and cites Venantius Fortunatus and Gregory of Tours alongside later abbey traditions.
The former Sacred Heart octave Wednesday page replaces unavailable Guéranger octave commentary with Pius XI's 1928 encyclical Miserentissimus Redemptor.

records.sourceTitle: Vigile de la fête de tous les Saints
records.observedSourceTopic: The Vigil of All Saints page expressly states suppression in 1955 and retains the old formulary for historical reading.
The Felix of Valois article itself reports historians disputing his existence because his name appears only in later Trinitarian foundation narratives.
Goëry is placed in Saint-Dié and older Toul local calendars, with an Arnulf connection and a healing legend in the historical presentation.
The local Saint Euchaire source presents a shared Toul-family genealogy with Élophe, Libaire and Menne, repeatedly hosted across individual siblings' articles.
Saint Libaire's article repeats the Toul-family story and places her cult in Saint-Dié/Nancy-Toul local calendars; martyrdom narrative should be tested separately.
Saint Menne's page repeats the same large Toul-family account, but describes Menne as consecrated virgin rather than simply treating all siblings as martyrs.
The Arbogast of Strasbourg article claims monastic foundations and expressly concedes his Haguenau forest hermitage belongs to legend.
The Gengoult text narrates the courtier's wife's infidelity and a water ordeal, presenting devotional hagiography rather than independent eighth-century biography.
The August 17 octave of St Lawrence article says this particular octave had disappeared in 1955, discussing earlier Roman sacramentary evidence and displaced St Hyacinth rankings.

records.sourceTitle: 30 décembre (6ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Nativité)
records.observedSourceTopic: The December 30 Nativity octave page contains Guéranger's comparison of the Christmas octave's many saint feasts against other octave structures.
The French-local St Louis page hosts two Francis de Sales outlines of a panegyric, explicitly noting plans not drafted out as full sermons.
Saint Amon is represented as the second bishop of Toul from local chronicles and later sources, in a diocesan observance described as ending there in 1955.

records.sourceTitle: Commun d’un Martyr Pontife hors du Temps Pascal Sacerdótes Dei
records.observedSourceTopic: Parsch explains the Sacerdotes Dei Bishop Martyr Common using an Introit from the Song of the Three Young Men rather than assuming an ordinary psalm.

records.sourceTitle: Commun d’un Martyr non Pontife hors du Temps Pascal Lætábitur iustus
records.observedSourceTopic: Parsch expounds the Laetabitur iustus non-bishop martyr common using its Psalm 63 and Pauline imprisonment Epistle.

records.sourceTitle: Commun d’un Confesseur non Pontife Iustus ut palma
records.observedSourceTopic: Parsch explicitly distinguishes two separate non-bishop Confessor formularies: vigilant-servant expectation versus ascetic self-renunciation.
Parsch comments on Cognovi as a common for non-martyr holy women, connecting interior prayer and household/maternal activity.

records.sourceTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi I Avent
records.observedSourceTopic: The Advent Saturday Marian formulary hosts historical discussion of Marian Saturday devotion and seasonal Marian texts.

records.sourceTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi II de la Nativité au 2 février
records.observedSourceTopic: The Nativity-to-February-2 Saturday Marian article reproduces the same historical introduction as the Advent version while identifying a different seasonal Mass.

records.sourceTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi III du 3 février au Mercredi Saint
records.observedSourceTopic: The February-to-Holy-Wednesday Marian Saturday article again repeats the general history while assigning its own season-specific Mass.

records.sourceTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi IV Temps Pascal
records.observedSourceTopic: The Paschal-season Marian Saturday article has the same general background as adjacent versions but a distinct Eastertide seasonal scope.

records.sourceTitle: Messes de la Sᵗᵉ Vierge le Samedi V Temps après la Pentecôte
records.observedSourceTopic: The post-Pentecost Marian Saturday article shares the boilerplate introduction but has a distinct period designation.
Alix Le Clerc's biography locates her Lorraine school foundation with Pierre Fourier, the first school at Poussay and the Congregation of Notre-Dame.
The Blessed Margaret of Lorraine account lists diocesan jurisdictions and her dynastic links to René II and René of Alençon.

records.sourceTitle: Commun d’un Martyr hors du Temps Pascal II : Sacerdótes Dei
records.observedSourceTopic: An older Sacerdotes Dei martyr Common repeats the same Parsch commentary seen in the newer article, not a second independent author witness.

records.sourceTitle: Commun d’un Martyr hors du Temps Pascal IV : Lætábitur
records.observedSourceTopic: An older Laetabitur martyr Common repeats Parsch's martyrdom meditation from the newer non-bishop martyr Common.
The Twelve Brother Martyrs article dates the commemorated event to a later Benevento relic translation, distinguishing it from an uncertain date of martyrdom.

records.sourceTitle: Sts Corneille, pape, et Cyprien, évêque, martyrs
records.observedSourceTopic: The Cornelius and Cyprian presentation says their joint feast was shifted from September 14 to 16 in the medieval calendar and identifies their distinct martyrdom years.
The Translation of Nicholas page relates the 1087 Bari removal and subsequent Lorraine cult at Saint-Nicolas-de-Port, explicitly treating the removal scene as legendary.
The Ascension-octave Monday article says the octave was suppressed in 1955 yet reproduces former Matins readings and Guéranger devotion.
The post-1955 Pentecost Vigil page describes six Old Testament prophecies and baptismal water ceremonies as an earlier usage removed by the 1955 reform.
Saint Gauzelin's local biography links the bishop of Toul with a foundation at Bouxières-aux-Dames and his burial there.
The diocesan text identifies Bodon or Leudin as seventeenth bishop of Toul and attributes the Etival foundation to tradition.
The Easter Vigil page explicitly identifies the reformed Pius XII rite and points to separate pre-1951 Holy Saturday commentaries.

records.sourceTitle: Jeudi de la 3ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.observedSourceTopic: Third-Advent Thursday presentation includes St Thomas December 21 precedence, Advent commemoration and Office antiphons in an explicitly date-dependent setting.

records.sourceTitle: Mardi de la 4ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.observedSourceTopic: Fourth-Advent Tuesday presentation repeats a note about St Thomas on December 21 and calls it the third Advent week even though the article is labelled fourth Advent week.

records.sourceTitle: Mercredi de la 4ᵉ semaine de l’Avent
records.observedSourceTopic: Fourth-Advent Wednesday repeats the same third-week St Thomas December 21 note, indicating a second date/rubric editorial-copy discrepancy.
The Good Friday source explicitly presents pre-Pius-XII ceremonies and points separately to commentary and Salesian sermon outlines.

records.sourceTitle: Féries du Temps de l’Epiphanie (du 7 au 12 janvier)
records.observedSourceTopic: The Jan 7–12 Epiphany ferial page distinguishes use of the Epiphany or post-Epiphany Sunday Mass with differing Gloria, Credo and Communicantes treatment.
Funeral-day Mass commentary emphasizes intercession for the deceased and specific treatment of baptized children below age of reason.
Daily Requiem Mass article cites the Catechism of the Council of Trent on the Mass's application to departed souls.
Transferred third after Epiphany Sunday combines chants from the twenty-third after Pentecost with its own prayers and Scripture readings.
Transferred fifth after Epiphany Sunday also combines the twenty-third Pentecost Sunday chants with different Epistle, Gospel and orations.
The post-1955 Holy Thursday article specifies solemn evening Mass within a stated afternoon/evening time window.

records.sourceTitle: Féries du Temps de la Nativité (2 au 5 janvier)
records.observedSourceTopic: Nativity ferial article retains the Puer natus est nobis Introit and distinguishes a seasonal Mass from the following named feast.
The page reproduces Paul VI's 1965 Eucharistic encyclical Mysterium Fidei, not commentary on a 1962 proper or rubric.
The votive Mass of Peter article says it may be offered separately from Paul while retaining a Pauline commemoration.

records.sourceTitle: Féries dans l’octave de la Nativité
records.observedSourceTopic: The Nativity-octave ferial page directs readers to December 30 for its commentary, rather than adding independent explanation.
The Holy Thursday article expressly presents the earlier pre-Pius-XII Mass and ceremonial form, separate from the revised evening Mass.
